title: Bank Mandiri Posts Rp 45.5 Trillion Net Profit in Q3 2026, Third-Party Funds Grow 17.7% to Rp 1,750.2 Trillion
body: Bank Mandiri reported consolidated net profit of Rp 45.5 trillion through Q3 2026, up 20.7% year on year, driven by ecosystem-based credit expansion, rising digital transactions, and improving business productivity. Loans (bank only) reached Rp 1,605.8 trillion, up 16% YoY, while third-party funds grew 17.7% YoY to Rp 1,750.2 trillion and total assets rose 20.1% YoY to Rp 2,404.1 trillion. Profitability strengthened with a cost-to-income ratio improving to 36.1%, return on equity of 23.6%, return on assets of 2.99%, and gross NPL (bank only) improving to 0.98%, supported by a capital adequacy ratio of 18.4%. The bank distributed Rp 50.6 trillion in dividends during 2026, including a Rp 6.16 trillion interim dividend, and its Livin' by Mandiri app recorded 42.6 million registered users with 4.18 billion transactions worth Rp 3,863 trillion from January to September 2026.

title: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) Confirms Healthy Capital Adequacy After Paying Rp 6.16 Trillion Interim Dividend
body: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) reported a Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) of 18.4 percent after paying an interim dividend of Rp 6.16 trillion on October 2, 2026. Finance & Strategy Director Novita Widya Anggraini said the capital ratio remains healthy despite the shareholder payout, with a positive trend month to month. Dividend decisions, both annual and interim, consider capital resilience, liquidity, and the need to support business growth, with the interim payment framed as appreciation to shareholders including retail investors. Bank Mandiri is committed to maintaining CAR in the 18-19 percent range to balance credit growth, risk profile, and capital formation.

title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Posts Rp 45.5 Trillion Net Profit in First Nine Months of 2026, Sucor Sekuritas Raises Target Price to Rp 4,350
body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) booked a net profit of Rp 45.5 trillion in the first nine months of 2026, up 20.7% year-on-year, including Rp 15.1 trillion in the July-September quarter, which grew 13.9% annually and 0.6% quarterly. Nine-month net interest income rose 6.5% year-on-year, non-interest income grew 14.3%, operating expenses fell 1.6%, and pre-provisioning operating profit increased 17.5% to Rp 21.5 trillion, although net interest margin slipped to 4.43% from 4.56% in the first half as deposit cost of fund rose to 2.34%. Asset quality remained broadly solid with gross non-performing loans stable at 1.02% and a 235% NPL coverage ratio, though loan at risk rose to 6.76% from 5.83% due to restructuring of performing loans in several state-owned enterprise construction and logistics exposures. Sucor Sekuritas projects Bank Mandiri's net profit at Rp 57 trillion for 2026 and Rp 57.2 trillion for 2027, raised its target price for BMRI shares to Rp 4,350 implying a 1.1 times price-to-book value on 2027 estimates, and maintained a hold recommendation, with the stock closing up 1.3% at Rp 3,900 on Friday, October 23, 2026.

title: Samuel Sekuritas Maintains Buy on PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) After Q3-2026 Results, Sets Rp 4,900 Target Price
body: Samuel Sekuritas Indonesia maintained its buy recommendation on PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) with a target price of Rp 4,900, implying 25.6% upside, based on a price-to-book value of 1.4 times for 2026 projections. Bank Mandiri's nine-month 2026 net profit reached Rp 45.5 trillion, up 20.7% year-on-year and fulfilling 80% of the Bloomberg analyst consensus of Rp 57.2 trillion for full-year 2026, while Q3-2026 net profit rose 13.9% year-on-year to Rp 15.1 trillion. Q3-2026 total operating income grew 6.7% year-on-year to Rp 34.9 trillion, with non-interest income up 10% quarter-on-quarter to Rp 12.7 trillion on treasury income growth of 27.6% and commission-based income of 8%, though net interest income fell 3.6% quarter-on-quarter to Rp 22 trillion due to a 20.7% rise in interest expenses. Loans reached Rp 1,694 trillion as of September 2026, up 15.4% year-on-year, third-party funds grew 17.5% to Rp 1,805 trillion with a 70.6% cheap funds ratio, while the nine-month net interest margin declined 35 basis points to 4.43%, the non-performing loan ratio stood at 1.02%, and the loan-at-risk ratio rose 93 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 6.76%.

title: Popular News Roundup: Anthoni Salim Issuers Announce Buybacks as Kiwoom Sekuritas Cuts Year-End IHSG Target
body: This roundup of investor.id's five most popular stories as of Saturday, October 24, 2026, is anchored by conglomerate Anthoni Salim's two issuers, PT Indofood Sukses Makmur Tbk (INDF) and PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk (ICBP), announcing share buyback plans amid market volatility following the MSCI announcement on possible reclassification of Indonesian equities. Kiwoom Sekuritas cut its year-end 2026 IHSG target from 7,000 to 5,700–6,000, citing MSCI pressure, foreign investor outflows, and market recovery uncertainty. PT Antam Tbk (ANTM) held its gold price steady at Rp 2,540,000 per gram, with a buyback price of Rp 2,335,000 per gram, on Saturday, October 24, 2026. PT Gudang Garam Tbk (GGRM) recorded net foreign buying from October 15 to 23, 2026, including Rp 24.3 billion on October 16 when the IHSG plunged 11.57%, while PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) jumped 15% during October 19–23, 2026, lifted by domestic net buying of Rp 1.36 trillion at an average price of Rp 3,564, and closed up 1.3% at Rp 3,900 on Friday, October 23, 2026.

title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Shares Rebound 15.04% in a Week After MSCI-Driven Slump, Backed by Domestic Net Buy and Strong Q3-2026 Earnings
body: Shares of PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) rebounded 15.04% during the trading week of October 19–23, 2026, after falling 14.82% on October 16, 2026, amid market turmoil following MSCI's announcement of a consultation on Indonesia's reclassification. On Friday, October 23, 2026, the stock rose 1.30% to Rp 3,900, with domestic investors recording a net buy of Rp 1.36 trillion at an average price of Rp 3,564, alongside trading of 255.52 million shares worth Rp 985.52 billion. The recovery was supported by the state-owned bank's consolidated net profit of Rp 45.5 trillion through Q3-2026, up 20.7% year on year, driven by ecosystem-based credit expansion, growing digital transactions, and improving business productivity. As of September 2026, bank-only loans reached Rp 1,605.8 trillion (+16% yoy), third-party funds Rp 1,750.2 trillion (+17.7% yoy), and total assets Rp 2,404.1 trillion (+20.1% yoy), while the company distributed Rp 50.6 trillion in dividends during 2026, including a Rp 6.16 trillion interim dividend for fiscal year 2026.

title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Posts Rp 45.5 Trillion Bank-Only Net Profit Through Q3 2026, Up 20.7% Year-on-Year
body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) recorded a bank-only net profit of Rp 45.5 trillion through the third quarter of 2026, growing 20.7% compared with the same period last year, driven by loan expansion and higher income. Consolidated total assets reached Rp 2,404.1 trillion, up 20.1% annually, while bank-only loans grew 16% year-on-year to Rp 1,605.83 trillion and third-party funds (DPK) rose 17.7% to Rp 1,750 trillion. Asset quality improved as the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio fell to 0.98% from 1.03% in September 2025, and the bank-only loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) stood at 91.2%, down from 92.6% a year earlier. Finance & Strategy Director Novita W. Anggraini said deposit growth remains the top priority given challenging liquidity conditions, and the company distributed Rp 50.6 trillion in dividends during 2026, including a Rp 6.16 trillion interim dividend for fiscal year 2026.

title: Bank Mandiri Net Profit Grows 20.7% to Rp45.5 Trillion Through September 2026
body: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) reported consolidated net profit of Rp45.5 trillion through September 2026, up 20.7% year on year, supported by healthy loan growth, rising digital transactions, and improving productivity. Bank-only loans grew 16% year on year to Rp1,606 trillion, while third-party funds rose 17.7% year on year, lifting the average daily loan-to-deposit ratio to 94.8% in Q3 2026 from 93.6% a year earlier. Asset quality improved as the non-performing loan ratio fell from 1.03% to 0.98%, with loans to the government and state-owned enterprise ecosystem up 23.8% to Rp473 trillion, the economic backbone ecosystem up 18.5% to Rp910 trillion, and micro loans up 12.9% to Rp31.2 trillion across 37 provinces. The Livin' by Mandiri app added about 20,000 new users daily with active user growth of around 13% year on year, and the bank has distributed Rp50.6 trillion in dividends during 2026.

title: Bank Mandiri Maintains Consistent Dividends and Buyback Program Backed by Solid Fundamentals
body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) views its share buyback as part of a routine capital management strategy to create long-term shareholder value, with the latest program repurchasing 91.75 million shares later allocated to an employee stock ownership program from June 24-29, 2026, per RUPST 2026 approval and OJK rules. Across 2026, Bank Mandiri distributed total dividends of about Rp50.63 trillion, consisting of Rp44.47 trillion from fiscal year 2025 and a Rp6.16 trillion interim dividend for fiscal year 2026. Finance & Strategy Director Novita Widya Anggraini said the interim dividend reflects appreciation for shareholders and the bank's earnings capability while balancing capital needs for expansion. Through August 2026, bank-only lending grew 17.6% YoY to Rp1,592 trillion, matched by third-party funds (DPK) of Rp1,687 trillion, also up 17.6% YoY and above industry growth of 13.7%. Asset quality remained intact with a gross NPL of 1.00%, an NPL coverage ratio of 240.6%, and bank-only net profit of Rp37.5 trillion, up 22.3% YoY.

title: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) to Distribute Rp 50.63 Trillion in Dividends Throughout 2026
body: PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) will distribute total dividends of approximately Rp 50.63 trillion throughout 2026, comprising Rp 44.47 trillion for fiscal year 2025 and an interim dividend of Rp 6.16 trillion for fiscal year 2026. Finance & Strategy Director Novita Widya Anggraini said the interim dividend is a form of appreciation to shareholders and reflects the bank's earnings capability, while remaining mindful of capital needs for expansion and risk anticipation. Beyond dividends, the bank completed a buyback of 91.75 million shares, which were transferred to employees through an Employee Stock Ownership Program held on 24-29 June 2026, in line with the 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPST) approval and OJK regulations. The company stated that dividends and buybacks are part of its capital management strategy to create long-term shareholder value while maintaining business resilience and expansion capacity.

title: 19 State-Owned Enterprise Stocks Close Higher Amid Massive Buying and Buyback Programs
body: Nineteen state-owned enterprise (SOE) stocks closed higher across banking, telecommunications, construction, and energy sectors, supported by large-scale buying and share buyback programs. The biggest gainers included PT PP Properti Tbk (PPRO) up 7.14% to Rp15, PT Jasa Marga (Persero) Tbk (JSMR) up 5.11% to Rp2,470, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI) up 4.92% to Rp3,410, and PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI) up 4.05% to Rp3,850, while PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) rose 4.41% to Rp2,840. BBRI, BMRI, PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), BBNI, and ANTM helped lift the IHSG, which closed up 1.12% at 5,387.91 on volume of 331.29 million lots worth Rp15.31 trillion. BMRI allocated Rp1.17 trillion for a buyback running April 30, 2026 to April 29, 2027, BBNI allocated Rp627 billion for July 27 to October 26, 2026, and Telkom moved to accelerate its Rp4 trillion buyback approved at the June 8, 2026 AGM, with over Rp3 trillion remaining as of October 19, 2026. BPI Danantara Indonesia, through Chief Investment Officer Pandu Sjahrir, said it has begun buying Indonesian stocks, viewing current market pressure on the IHSG as an investment opportunity and planning to increase holdings in SOE stocks citing strong fundamentals and attractive valuations.

title: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) Buybacks 91.75 Million Shares, Total 2026 Dividends Reach Rp 50.63 Trillion
body: PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (BMRI) reaffirmed its share buyback strategy as part of capital management and long-term shareholder value creation, having repurchased 91.75 million shares in its latest program. The buyback shares were allocated to the Employee Stock Ownership Program on June 24-29, 2026, in line with the 2026 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders approval and Financial Services Authority (OJK) rules. The bank also distributed total dividends of about Rp 50.63 trillion across the 2026 calendar, comprising Rp 44.47 trillion from fiscal year 2025 and Rp 6.16 trillion in interim dividends for fiscal year 2026. Supporting performance through August 2026 (bank only) includes loans of Rp 1,592 trillion (+17.6% YoY), third-party funds of Rp 1,687 trillion (+17.6% YoY), gross NPL of 1.00%, NPL coverage ratio of 240.6%, and net profit of Rp 37.5 trillion (+22.3% YoY).

title: IHSG Turns Green Supported by State-Owned Enterprise Stocks Amid Buyback Programs and Danantara Entry Plans
body: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) rose 53.07 points or 1% to 5,381.43 at 09:56 WIB during mid-morning trading, after falling as much as 2% at the open, supported mainly by state-owned enterprise (BUMN) stocks including PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk (BMRI), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBRI), PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM), PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (BBNI), and PT Aneka Tambang (Persero) Tbk (ANTM). The rebound coincided with multiple issuers on the Indonesia Stock Exchange conducting share buybacks from October to December 2026: Bank Mandiri allocated Rp1.17 trillion for the period April 30, 2026 to April 29, 2027, Bank Negara Indonesia allocated Rp627 billion for July 27, 2026 to October 26, 2026, and Telkom is accelerating its buyback of up to Rp4 trillion approved at the June 8, 2026 annual shareholders meeting, with more than Rp3 trillion remaining as of October 19, 2026. Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani called the share price decline a long-term investment opportunity, while COO Dony Oskaria, who also heads BP BUMN, opened the possibility of increasing BUMN share ownership, though Danantara has not specified which stocks or amounts. Investors are also watching whether the gains hold following heavy selling two days earlier and awaiting MSCI's decision on Indonesia's market status.

title: Trillions of Rupiah Ready to Enter the Market as 10 Issuers Prepare Rp 18.6 Trillion Share Buybacks, BRI Danareksa Sekuritas Says
body: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas (BRIDS) notes that at least 10 issuers are preparing share buyback programs totaling up to Rp 18.6 trillion, adding demand-side support amid market volatility. Five new programs worth Rp 4.5 trillion from DSSA, BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN began between October 19-23, shortly after the market correction on October 16, providing about Rp 1.8 trillion of support per month over 2-3 months. Companies affiliated with Prajogo lead with Rp 3.5 trillion, as BREN, BRPT, TPIA, and CUAN hold 78% of the new program funds, active until December 31, 2026. Large banks have committed Rp 10.1 trillion, or 54% of the total, with BBCA the largest at Rp 5.0 trillion, followed by BBRI at Rp 3.0 trillion, while annual programs from BBCA, TLKM, BMRI, and BBNI run at about Rp 0.9 trillion per month. BRIDS notes that buyback values are maximum limits and actual realization may be smaller.
